outcomeNote: a mishna stating two rulings; no argument, no dispute, no named parties.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַשּׁוֹחֵט לְשֵׁם הָרִים, לְשֵׁם גְּבָעוֹת, לְשֵׁם יַמִּים, לְשֵׁם נְהָרוֹת, לְשֵׁם מִדְבָּרוֹת – שְׁחִיטָתוֹ פְּסוּלָה.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In the case of «one who slaughters» an animal «for the sake of,» i.e., to worship, «mountains, for the sake of hills, for the sake of seas, for the sake of rivers,» or «for the sake of wildernesses, his slaughter is not valid.»

segments.he: שְׁנַיִם אוֹחֲזִין בְּסַכִּין וְשׁוֹחֲטִין, אֶחָד לְשֵׁם אֶחָד מִכׇּל אֵלּוּ וְאֶחָד לְשֵׁם דָּבָר כָּשֵׁר – שְׁחִיטָתוֹ פְּסוּלָה.
segments.en: If there were «two» people «grasping a knife» together «and slaughtering» an animal, «one» slaughtering «for the sake of one of all those» enumerated in the first clause of the mishna «and one» slaughtering «for the sake of a legitimate matter,» their «slaughter is not valid.»

moves.summary: the mishna rules that slaughter for the sake of natural entities is invalid
the mishna extends the rule to two joint slaughterers where only one has the disqualifying intent
